title: Integrated AI and Wireless for Sustainable Mobile Network Evolutions
summary: The Venus project describes real-time AI prediction of ionospheric delay. A separate improvement in positioning or communication quality is not established.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The Venus project combines wireless infrastructure with AI functions. Its application scenarios include real-time AI prediction of ionospheric delay, which can affect radio-signal propagation and positioning. This record concerns that prediction application. The source does not quantify a resulting improvement in positioning or communication quality. Its separate chip, compiler, and open-source infrastructure gains are not treated as benefits produced by the prediction system.
purpose: Use AI to predict ionospheric delay in support of communications and positioning. The benefit remains intended.

ratings.reason: The source identifies real-time AI prediction as an application for communications research. It does not establish the extent of a resulting positioning or communication benefit. Hardware and compiler efficiency figures are not assigned to this AI application.

ai_role.statement: The source explicitly identifies real-time AI ionospheric-delay prediction. Its effect on positioning or communication outcomes is not separately evaluated in the entry.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 4: Integrated AI and Wireless for Sustainable Mobile Network Evolutions

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.
